sources: CRA — Classes of depreciable property (canada.ca, page modified 2026-08-31) · current · Class 50 (55%): general-purpose electronic data processing equipment and systems software; Class 12 (100%, tools under $500) specifically excludes electronic data processing equipment, so a laptop is Class 50 at any price
CRA — Accelerated investment incentive (canada.ca, modified 2025-07-21) · 2018–2027 · AIIP: acquired after Nov 20, 2018 and available for use before 2028; half-year rule effectively suspended

Budget 2025 Implementation Act, No. 1 (SC 2026, c. 3; Royal Assent March 26, 2026) amending Income Tax Regulations 1100(2) · 2024–2026 · description of A, para. (c.3): Class 50 property acquired and available for use after April 15, 2024 and before 2027 gets an extra 9/11 of the cost in year one → 55% × (1 + 9/11) = 100% first-year CCA; A.1 para. (e) the same for reaccelerated property, nil after 2026

Same Act, Regulations 1104(4.01) · 2025–2033 · reaccelerated investment incentive property: acquired after 2024, available for use before 2034 (not previously owned / non-arm's-length conditions); half-year rule not applied, so a Class 50 laptop in use in 2027 gets 55% in year one
CRA T4127 (Jan 2026) and CPP 2026, via b4/calc.py · 2026 · tax + CPP for the B4 freelancer (MB, single, $60,000 net): $16,105.48

Calculation (not a CRA rule): b11/calc.py → data.json. $2,000 laptop, 100% business use, MB single $60,000 net self-employment income, 2026 rates. In use in 2026: CCA $2,000 → saves $711.27 tax + CPP (35.6¢ per $1). In use in 2027: CCA $1,100 → saves $391.20 in year one (2026 rates used for comparison); the other $900 is claimed in later years at 55% declining balance ($495, $222.75, …). Dependencies: business-use share (mixed use → only the business part), the date the laptop is available for use, CCA is optional (any amount up to the maximum), province and income. Example only.

yt.description:
Can you write off a new laptop all at once? In 2026, yes. From January 2027, no.

Example: a Manitoba freelancer netting $60,000 buys a $2,000 laptop used only for work.
• A laptop is equipment: capital cost allowance, Class 50, normally 55% a year.
• Computers bought and put to use before 2027 get a 100% first-year claim: all $2,000. Saves about $711 in tax + CPP.
• Same laptop put to use in January 2027: year one is 55% = $1,100 (saves about $391); the other $900 comes in later years.

The honest part: spending $2,000 to save $711 is still spending. Buy it because you need it.

Sold the old laptop? There's a catch. Want it? Comment CATCH.

Sources: CRA CCA classes (Class 50); Income Tax Regulations 1100(2) as amended by the Budget 2025 Implementation Act, No. 1 (2026); CRA T4127 2026 rates, CPP 2026. Mixed use: only the business share. Example only; general information, not tax advice.
